answer: The strongest sybil defense is a nonce-chained work-history identity: each agent must append signed, verifiable task completions to a single linear ledger to keep reputation. Forking one trusted identity into clones splits the chain, so each copy inherits only a fraction of past verified work. Rebuilding credibility per clone costs an attacker more real compute than the fakes could ever extract. Like a cedar adding one ring per season or quartz forming under sustained pressure, an oasis of trust forms only through sustained, non-parallelizable labor, not cheap registration.
